*1 April: Malaysia's first nationwide automotive recall was announced due to defects in the [[Proton Savvy]]'s rear wheel [[Bearing (mechanical)|bearing]].<ref>{{cite web|author1=Paul Tan|author-link=Paul Tan|title=Proton Savvy rear wheel bearing recall|url=http://paultan.org/2008/03/31/proton-savvy-rear-wheel-bearing-recall/|website=Paultan.org|access-date=16 May 2016|date=March 31, 2008}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Proton recalls 34,000 Savvy cars|url=http://www.malaysia-today.net/proton-recalls-34000-savvy-cars/|publisher=[[Malaysia Today]]|access-date=16 May 2016|date=March 31, 2008|archive-date=12 October 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161012063127/http://www.malaysia-today.net/proton-recalls-34000-savvy-cars/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Affected restaurants include McDonald's and [[Mr. Sub]].
*September: 440,000 [[Sony]] [[vaio|VAIO]] type T TZ series due to excessive heat production, produced in May 2007 - July 2008 had to be recalled.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2008-09-04 |title=Sony recalls laptops for possible overheating |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/id/wbna26543514 |access-date=2025-10-26 |website=[[NBC News]] |language=en}}</ref>

===2009===
*January: [[Peanut Corporation of America]] recalled its bulk [[peanut butter]] and peanut paste products for salmonella contamination. Because of the myriad of consumer items PCA's bulk products went into, the [[Food and Drug Administration]] eventually recalled 3913 different products from at least 361 companies - one of the most extensive food recalls in US history. On February 13, 2009, [[Peanut Corporation of America]] filed for [[Chapter 7, Title 11, United States Code|Chapter 7 liquidation]] following the massive extensive peanut butter recall. In 2014, The United States Department of Justice criminally indicted Parnell and his family for committing at least 70 counts of felony wire and mail fraud after being unanimously found guilty of those charges by a federal grand jury. In September 2015, Stewart Parnell, who was the CEO of PCA at the time of the 2009 peanut butter recall, pleaded guilty to 70 felony charges of wire fraud and mail fraud. He was sentenced to 28 years in prison for mishandling the peanut butter recall in 2009 and for the felony wire fraud and mail fraud charges.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Silberner|first1=Joanne|title=Salmonella Outbreak Leads To Peanut Butter Recall|url=https://www.npr.org/templates/story/story.php?storyId=99341551|newspaper=[[NPR]]|access-date=14 May 2016|date=January 15, 2009}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=Reinberg|first1=Steven|title=More Than 200 Peanut Butter Products Now Under Recall|url=https://abcnews.go.com/Health/Healthday/story?id=6718643&page=1|access-date=14 May 2016|work=ABC News|date=January 24, 2009}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|author1=Daniel J. DeNoon|title=Salmonella Prompts Peanut Butter Recall|url=http://www.webmd.com/food-recipes/food-poisoning/20090114/salmonella-prompts-peanut-butter-recall|website=[[WebMD]]|access-date=14 May 2016|date=January 14, 2009}}</ref>
*March: Setton Pistachio of [[Terra Bella, California]] recalled its entire 2008 crop of [[pistachios]] due to salmonella contamination.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Martin|first1=Andrew|last2=Moss|first2=Michael|title=Salmonella in Pistachios Spurs Recall|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2009/03/31/business/31nuts.html|access-date=14 May 2016|work=The New York Times|date=March 30, 2009}}</ref>
*June: 300,000&nbsp;packages of [[Nestlé]]'s [[Chocolate chip cookie|Toll House cookie dough]] are recalled due to possible ''E. coli'' contamination that made several consumers sick, when the dough was eaten raw.<ref>{{cite news|author1=Reporting by Nicole Maestri|author2=Editing by Lisa Von Ahn|title=Nestlé recalls Toll House cookie dough after E. coli warning|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-nestle-idUSTRE55I3IG20090619|access-date=14 May 2016|work=Reuters|date=June 19, 2009}}</ref>
*October: Some [[Acer Aspire]] laptops were recalled for overheating problems.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Luo|first1=Serene|title=Acer laptops here hit by recall|url=http://www.straitstimes.com/Breaking+News/Singapore/Story/STIStory_441682.html|newspaper=[[The Straits Times]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091016065817/http://www.straitstimes.com/Breaking+News/Singapore/Story/STIStory_441682.html|archive-date=October 16, 2009|date=October 13, 2009}}</ref>
*December: Virtually every [[window blind#Roman|Roman blind]] and roller shade on the market—around 50 million sets—were recalled because the cords pose a strangulation hazard to children.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Leamy|first1=Elisabeth|last2=Weber|first2=Vanessa|title=50 Million Blinds Recalled Following Child Deaths|url=https://abcnews.go.com/GMA/ConsumerNews/50-million-blinds-recall-child-deaths/story?id=9336171|publisher=[[ABC News (United States)|ABC News]]|access-date=14 May 2016|date=December 15, 2009}}</ref>

The taste of the contaminated boxes was described as "stale, metal, and soap-like" by consumers.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://consumeralert.kelloggs.com/consumeralert.aspx?id=3870 |title=Kellogg's - Consumer Alert |publisher=Consumeralert.kelloggs.com |date=2010-06-25 |access-date=2012-11-03 |url-status=dead |archive-url=http://webarchive.loc.gov/all/20100820141826/http://consumeralert.kelloggs.com/consumeralert.aspx?id=3870 |archive-date=2010-08-20 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Fulton |first=April |date=2010-06-29 |title=Kellogg Recalls Popular Breakfast Cereals Because Of Strange Smell |url=https://www.npr.org/sections/health-shots/2010/06/29/128191629/kellogg-recalls-popular-breakfast-cereals-because-of-strange-smell |access-date=2026-01-20 |work=NPR |language=en}}</ref>
*July: [[Perdue Farms]] recalls over 90,000&nbsp;pounds of [[chicken nugget]]s after bits of blue plastic were found in the nuggets.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nydailynews.com/news/money/perdue-recalls-90-000-pounds-chicken-nuggets-finding-plastic-article-1.202547 |title=Perdue recalls 90,000+ pounds of chicken nuggets after finding plastic in some |work=New York Daily News |date=2010-07-20 |access-date=2021-11-13}}</ref>
*August: 228 million eggs are voluntarily recalled by [[Wright County Egg]] of [[Galt, Iowa]] due to a potential salmonella contamination.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fda.gov/newsevents/newsroom/pressannouncements/ucm223248.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100821081516/http://www.fda.gov/NewsEvents/Newsroom/PressAnnouncements/ucm223248.htm |url-status=dead |archive-date=August 21, 2010 |title=Urgent Nationwide Egg Recall |publisher=Fda.gov |access-date=2012-11-03}}</ref>
*September: [[Fisher-Price]] recalls 10&nbsp;million products, including enough toys to merit this as the largest toy recall in history.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://service.mattel.com/us/recall.asp |title=Mattel and Fisher-Price Consumer Relations Support Center - Product Recalls & Safety Alerts |publisher=Service.mattel.com |access-date=2012-11-03}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=Chernikoff|first1=Helen|last2=Bavdek|first2=Maureen|title=Mattel's Fisher-Price to recall 10 million products|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-fisherpricerecall-idUSTRE68T2ZB20100930|access-date=14 May 2016|work=Reuters|date=September 30, 2010}}</ref>
*September 23: [[Similac]]: [[Abbott Laboratories]] issued a voluntary recall of up to 5&nbsp;million containers of Similac infant formula after finding beetles in the formula.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://abcnews.go.com/Health/ParentingResourceCenter/similac-recall-bug-parts-baby-formula-worry-parents/story?id=11710959 |title=Similac Recall: Bug Parts in Baby Formula Worry Parents - ABC News |publisher=ABC News |date=2010-09-23 |access-date=2012-11-03}}</ref> ISSUE: Possibility of the presence of a small common beetle in the product. While the  U.S. [[Food and Drug Administration]] (FDA) determined that the formula containing these beetles posed no immediate health risk, there was a possibility that infants who consumed the formula could experience symptoms of gastrointestinal discomfort and refusal to eat as a result of small insect parts irritating the GI tract. The voluntary recall affected milk- and soy-based formulas distributed in the United States, Puerto Rico, Guam, and some Caribbean nations. At least 12 of the recalled products were provided to families through the federal government's Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) health and nutrition program. The FDA reassured caregivers and families whose babies may have consumed these products that drinking the formula will not cause long-term health problems.<ref>{{cite web|title=Similac Powder Infant Formulas: Recall|url=https://www.fda.gov/Safety/MedWatch/SafetyInformation/SafetyAlertsforHumanMedicalProducts/ucm226954.htm|publisher=[[Food and Drug Administration|FDA]]|access-date=14 May 2016|date=September 23, 2010}}{{dead link|date=May 2025|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>

===2011===
*January: Nature's Promise Giant Food of Landover, Md. issued a voluntary recall of several Nature's Promise organic bagged salad items due to the potential for ''[[listeria]]'' contamination. there was a report of a pregnant woman in her 20s being rushed to the hospital after eating tainted salad. No deaths reported.<ref>[http://www.myfoxny.com/dpp/your_money/recalls/natures-promise-salad-recall-20110126 Archived copy] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110201062114/http://www.myfoxny.com/dpp/your_money/recalls/natures-promise-salad-recall-20110126|date=February 1, 2011}}</ref>
*February: U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission issued a recall 20,000 of Sniglar Cribs, distributed by [[IKEA]] Home Furnishings due to the detach and collapse of the Mattress, creating a risk of entrapment and suffocation to a child in the crib.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.newsinferno.com/legal-news/ikea-cribs-recalled-for-entrapment-suffocation-hazard/ |title=IKEA Cribs Recalled for Entrapment, Suffocation Hazard |publisher=NewsInferno |date=2011-02-18 |access-date=2012-11-03 |archive-date=2012-07-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120723082222/http://www.newsinferno.com/legal-news/ikea-cribs-recalled-for-entrapment-suffocation-hazard |url-status=dead }}</ref>
*February: [[Honda]] Motor Company issued a voluntary safety recall of 700,000&nbsp;cars due to the failure. The spring was placed improperly in a small box inside the engine, so that, in some cases, the problem could cause the engine to stall. No crashes or injuries have been reported related to this defect.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nbcnews.com/id/wbna41641006 |title=Honda recalling nearly 700,000 small cars - Business - Autos |publisher=NBC News |date=2011-02-17 |access-date=2012-11-03}}</ref>
*February: Study on [[Medical device]] recall by Dr. [[Diana Zuckerman]] and Paul Brown of the [[National Center for Health Research|National Research Center for Women and Families]], and Dr. Steven Nissen of the [[Cleveland Clinic]], published in the Archives of Internal Medicine, showed that most medical devices recalled in the last five years for “serious health problems or death” had been previously approved by the U.S. [[Food and Drug Administration]] (FDA) using the less stringent, and cheaper, 501(k) process.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://archinte.ama-assn.org/cgi/content/full/archinternmed.2011.30 |title=JAMA Network &#124; Archives of Internal Medicine &#124; Medical Device Recalls and the FDA Approval ProcessMedical Device Recalls and FDA Approval Process |publisher=Archinte.ama-assn.org |access-date=2012-11-03 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120402143034/http://archinte.ama-assn.org/cgi/content/full/archinternmed.2011.30 |archive-date=2012-04-02 }}</ref>
*March: Toyota Motor Corp issued a recall about 22,000&nbsp;sport utility vehicles and pickup trucks over tire-deflation monitoring systems that could cause failure. No such crashes or injuries were reported.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-toyota-recall-idUSTRE7262WS20110307 | work=Reuters | first=Bernie | last=Woodall | title=Toyota recalls 22,000 vehicles over tire monitors | date=March 7, 2011}}</ref>
*March: [[Saputo Dairy UK|Dairy Crest]]  recalled one batch of its [[Frijj]] Thick and Fresh Strawberry milkshake due to low levels of listeria.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.food.gov.uk/news/newsarchive/2011/mar/frijj |title=Food Standards Agency - FRijj Strawberry Milkshake recalled |publisher=Food.gov.uk |access-date=2012-11-03 |archive-date=2012-05-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120520091735/http://food.gov.uk/news/newsarchive/2011/mar/frijj |url-status=dead }}</ref>

*November: [[Hotpoint]] and [[Indesit]] began alerting customers who had purchased a tumble dryer between 2004 and 2015 because of the risk of fluff and lint building up around the heating element and presenting a severe fire hazard. A fire occurred in London in August 2016 caused by a tumble dryer which was awaiting inspection after recall.<ref>BBC News, [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-london-37203933 Shepherd's Bush tower block fire caused by faulty tumble dryer], published 27 August 2016, accessed 30 August 2023</ref> The [[Government of the United Kingdom|UK government]] established a Working Group on Product Recalls and Safety after this event, aiming to "improve product safety and recalls to avoid similar events occurring in future".<ref>Gibbins, N., [https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/630206/wgprs-report-open-letter.pdf Open Letter to the Minister for Small Business, Consumers and Corporate Responsibility], published 19 July 2017, accessed 30 August 2023</ref>

===2020===
* UK: January 26: [[Cow & Gate]] and [[Tesco]] are recalling 15 types of baby food jars as a "precautionary measure" amid concerns some may have been tampered with.
* USA: July 9: 4E Brands North America, based out of San Antonio, issued a major recall on all of its hand sanitizers across the country that were sold under the Blumen and Assured brands due to containing methanol, which was an alcohol that can be deadly to humans if absorbed throughout the skin. Most, if not all, of these bottles were sold at Walmart, Costco, and BJ's Wholesale Club stores nationwide, mostly in the Northeast. Cases of blindness, hospitalizations, and deaths occurred after adults and children drank the products, which lead to many lawsuits. On February 23, 2022, 4E Brands filed for [[Chapter 11, Title 11, United States Code|Chapter 11 bankruptcy]] and shut down all operations permanently, nearly two years after the recall, citing the number of lawsuits it got during the recall.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cnn.com/2020/07/09/health/hand-sanitizer-methanol-fda-trnd/index.html|title=FDA warns against using two dozen hand sanitizers that could contain toxic wood alcohol|date=July 9, 2020|access-date=April 1, 2023|website=CNN|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2022-02-23/toxic-hand-sanitizer-triggers-bankruptcy-at-kimberly-s-4e-brands|title=Toxic hand sanitizer triggers bankruptcy mid lawsuits|date=February 23, 2022|access-date=April 1, 2023|website=Bloomberg|language=en}}</ref>
* USA: July 23: [[Target Corporation|Target]] recalls [[Manhattan]] Teether toy due to risks of Choking hazard.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.kalb.com/2020/07/22/teether-toy-sold-at-target-recalled-over-choking-hazard |title=Teether toy sold at Target recalled over choking hazard |work=KALB |access-date=2020-07-25}}</ref> ISSUE: [[U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission]] is asking the people who bought the item to keep the toy away from children and return it to any Target store for a full refund.
* Europe: September: [[Ethylene oxide#2020 sesame seeds contamination|Sesame seeds contamination]] by ethylene oxide.
* Philippines: September 10: The [[Philippines|Philippine]] [[National Telecommunications Commission]] issued an order to recall frequencies and-channels assigned to [[ABS-CBN]], [[shutdown of ABS-CBN broadcasting|citing the absence of the latter's valid, legislative franchise]].
* Canada: October: Certain lots of [[Cottonelle]]-branded flushable wipes were recalled due to being contaminated with ''[[Pluralibacter gergoviae]]''.<ref>{{cite web |title=Cottonelle® & Cottonelle® GentlePlus Flushable Wipes Products recalled due to potential microbial contamination |url=https://healthycanadians.gc.ca/recall-alert-rappel-avis/hc-sc/2020/74165r-eng.php |website=Health Canada |date=20 October 2020 |publisher=October 21, 2020 |access-date=26 April 2021}}</ref>
* Worldwide: McDonald's and Disney announced the recall of all [[Mickey & Minnie's Runaway Railway]] toys due to a QR code error, bringing generic toys instead and removing tickets to [[Walt Disney World]].{{citation needed|date=June 2024}}

===2021===
* USA: January 4: Target recalls 181,000 Cat and Jack children's swimsuits due to the snaps breaking causing a choking hazard.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://abc7.com/target-recall-cat-and-jack-romper-cloud-island-infant/9358566/ |title=Target recalls infant rompers, swimsuits due to choking hazard |work=ABC News |date=5 January 2021 |access-date= 2021-01-30}}</ref>
* USA: January: 700,000 [[Hot Pockets]] were recalled due to bits of glass and plastic being reported in the pockets.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2021/01/16/us/hot-pockets-recall-trnd/index.html |title=Hot Pockets recalled over potential glass and plastic contamination |work=CNN |date=16 January 2021 |access-date= 2021-01-30}}</ref>
* USA: April: U.S. officials recall and suspend the use of the [[Johnson & Johnson]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|coronavirus vaccine]] due to blood clots being reported in women who received the vaccine.
* USA: April 10: The [[Food and Drug Administration]] stated that [[Hostess Brands|Hostess]] announced a recall on all of its [[Sno Balls]] treats after the treats tested positive for an unknown undeclared allergen.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://bestlifeonline.com/news-hostess-snack-recall/|title = The FDA is Warning You Not to Eat This Beloved Hostess Snack| work=Best Life |date = 12 April 2021 | last1=Crow | first1=Sarah }}</ref>
* USA: April 14: The FDA issued a recall on all of [[Trader Joe's]] Restaurant Style White Corn Tortilla Chips due to possible contamination of undeclared dairy. The contaminated chips were produced by [[Snak King]]. The recalled chips were removed from the market after it was discovered that the chips were contaminated with undeclared dairy.<ref>{{cite web |title=Snak King Corporation Issues Allergy Alert on Undeclared Milk Allergen in Trader Joe's Restaurant Style White Corn Tortilla Chips |url=https://www.fda.gov/safety/recalls-market-withdrawals-safety-alerts/snak-king-corporation-issues-allergy-alert-undeclared-milk-allergen-trader-joes-restaurant-style |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210414182820/https://www.fda.gov/safety/recalls-market-withdrawals-safety-alerts/snak-king-corporation-issues-allergy-alert-undeclared-milk-allergen-trader-joes-restaurant-style |url-status=dead |archive-date=April 14, 2021 |website=FDA.gov |publisher=April 14, 2021 |access-date=25 April 2021}}</ref>
* Worldwide: May: [[Hyundai Motor Company]] recalled the [[Hyundai Elantra|Elantra]], [[Hyundai Kona|Kona]], and [[Hyundai Veloster|Veloster]] models with a 2.0-liter engine to address a potential issue with the piston rings. The concern is that the problem could lead to increased oil consumption, progressing to a knocking sound, and the engine seizing and stalling.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.consumerreports.org/car-recalls-defects/hyundai-elantra-kona-veloster-recalled-due-to-engine-problems-a1121205321/ |title=Hyundai Elantra, Kona, and Veloster Recalled Due to Engine Problems |work=Consumer Reports |date=4 May 2021 |access-date=2021-10-08}}</ref>
* USA: July: [[Johnson & Johnson]] issued a major recall on its [[Aveeno]] and [[Neutrogena]] sunscreens after independent testing had found that they were contaminated with benzene, a cancer-causing chemical that could also develop leukemia and other blood disorders is exposed to it, according to the [[National Cancer Institute]]. Some [[CVS Health]] sunscreens were also recalled for the same reason.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cnn.com/2021/07/17/health/sunscreen-recall-cancer-wellness/index.html|title=Sunscreen recall: What the finding of a cancer-causing chemical means for you|date=July 17, 2021|access-date=April 1, 2023|website=CNN|language=en}}</ref>
* USA: July: various branded muffin names from the Give and Go Prepared Foods Corporation that were sold at various retailers including Walmart, 7-Eleven, Sam's Club, BJ's Wholesale Club, and Stop & Shop, were recalled for possible listeria contamination.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/money/shopping/2021/07/21/muffin-recall-walmart-great-value-7-eleven-listeria-contamination/8043761002/|title=Muffin recall 2021: Walmart, Sam's Club, 7-Eleven sold muffins recalled for listeria contamination|date=July 21, 2021|access-date=April 1, 2023|website=USA Today|language=en}}</ref>
* Germany: September: The KBA ordered a recall of about 200,000 [[Volkswagen Transporter (T6)|Volkswagen T6.1]] transporters, multivans, caravelles and California campervans that were built between 2019 and 2021. German authorities said that penetrating water at temperatures below freezing point could impair the door locking mechanism, making it appear as though the doors were locked, creating a risk that they could open unexpectedly while driving.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/autos-transportation/kba-orders-recall-200000-vw-t6-multivans-over-door-locking-mechanism-2021-09-30/ |title=KBA orders recall of 200,000 VW T6 multivans over door-locking mechanism |work=Reuters |date=30 September 2021 |publisher=September 30, 2021 |access-date=December 10, 2021}}</ref>
* USA: October: [[Walmart]] recalls The Better Homes & Gardens Lavender & Chamomile Essential Oil Infused Aromatherapy Room Spray with Gemstones, after a product sample tested positive for ''[[Burkholderia pseudomallei]]'', a deadly bacterial infection resulting in 2 deaths.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.foxbusiness.com/lifestyle/recalled-walmart-product-contaminated-with-rare-bacteria-cdc-finds |title=Recalled Walmart product tests positive for deadly bacteria |work=Fox Business |date=26 October 2021 |publisher=October 26, 2021 |access-date=October 30, 2021}}</ref>
* USA: November 16: several flavors of Country Time, Tang, Arizona Tea, and Kool-Aid powders were recalled due to the possibility of them containing metal or glass in them. The products were sold at many retailers, including Walmart, Sam's Club, Costco, and Target.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cbs19news.com/story/45283976/koolaid-tang-other-powdered-drinks-recalled-may-contain-metal-or-glass|title=Kool-Aid, Tang, other powdered drinks recalled; may contain metal or glass|date=November 24, 2021|access-date=April 1, 2023|website=CBS 19 News|language=en}}</ref>
* Worldwide: December 3: [[Honda]] Motor Company issued a major recall of 789,000 SUVs and pickup trucks because the [[Hood (car)|hood]] could open by itself while the car was in motion, heightening the risk of an accident. It covers certain [[Honda Passport|2019 Passports]], 2016 through [[Honda Pilot|2019 Pilots]] and 2017 through [[Honda Ridgeline|2020 Ridgeline]] pickups.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/honda-recall-suvs-pickups-hoods-fly-open/ |title=Honda recalls SUVs and pickups because hoods can fly open at high speeds |work=CBS News |date=3 December 2021 |publisher=December 3, 2021 |access-date=December 5, 2021}}</ref>
* USA: December 10: [[The Coca-Cola Company]] recalled [[Minute Maid]] products due to the potential presence of foreign matter, specifically metal bolts or washers.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/money/food/2021/12/13/coca-cola-minute-maid-recall/6488217001/ |title=Minute Maid products recalled in 8 states over concerns of foreign metal objects |work=USA Today |publisher=December 13, 2021 |access-date=December 21, 2021}}</ref>
* USA: December 21: [[Procter & Gamble|P&G]] Co. issued a voluntary recall of a variety of aerosol haircare products, after [[benzene]], a cancer-causing chemical, was detected in some stores. The affected products include dry shampoos and dry conditioners from [[Pantene]], Aussie and Herbal Essences, produced in the U.S.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.wsj.com/amp/articles/p-g-recalls-some-pantene-aussie-herbal-essences-dry-shampoos-11640038718 |title=P&G Recalls Dozens of Pantene, Aussie, Herbal Essences Dry Shampoos |work=The Wall Street Journal |date=21 December 2021 |publisher=December 21, 2021 |access-date=December 21, 2021|last1=Ansari |first1=Talal }}</ref>
* USA: December 27: [[Dole plc]] recalls its packaged salad processed in the company's [[Bessemer City, North Carolina]] and [[Yuma, Arizona]] production facilities due to possible ''[[listeria monocytogenes]]'' contamination.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wsbradio.com/news/trending/dole-fresh-express-recall-packaged-salad-over-concerns-about-listeria/DHQZEHM6VNEGBNATDKTASSJ3IE/ |title=Dole, Fresh Express recall packaged salad over concerns about listeria |last=Lord |first=Debbie |work=WSB Radio |date=27 December 2021 |publisher=December 27, 2021 |access-date = December 31, 2021}}</ref>

* Indonesia: March: [[Panasonic]] storage water heaters (DH-15HCMRW, DH-30HCMRW, DH-30HCDRW) are recalled due to safety issues, namely an electric shock that lead to the death of a family in [[Pulo Gadung]], [[East Jakarta]], whilst using the hot shower.
* Canada, USA: April: [[Kinder Chocolate|Kinder brand chocolate]] products were recalled due to possible ''[[Salmonella]]'' contamination.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-04-11 |title=Certain Kinder brand chocolate products recalled due to possible Salmonella |url=https://recalls-rappels.canada.ca/en/alert-recall/certain-kinder-brand-chocolate-products-recalled-due-possible-salmonella-0 |access-date=2022-05-31 |website=Recalls, advisories and safety alerts – Canada.ca |publisher=Health Canada, Government of Canada }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-04-09 |title=Kinder recalls Chocolates over microbiological concerns |url=https://club.flappd.ca/t/kinder-recalls-chocolates-over-microbiological-concerns/160 |access-date=2022-05-31 |website=Club Flappd |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-04-12 |title=Ferrero Voluntarily Recalls Kinder® Happy Moments Chocolate Assortment and Kinder® Mix Chocolate Treats Basket Because of Possible Health Risk and Advises Consumers to Dispose of Certain Kinder Products Not Intended for U.S. Distribution Due to Recall of Products Made in Belgium |url=https://www.fda.gov/safety/recalls-market-withdrawals-safety-alerts/ferrero-voluntarily-recalls-kinderr-happy-moments-chocolate-assortment-and-kinderr-mix-chocolate |access-date=2022-05-31 |website=U.S. Food and Drug Administration |location=Center for Food Safety and Applied Nutrition |language=en}}</ref>

* Canada, USA: May: It was announced on May 30 that HEB and FreshKampo [[strawberry|strawberries]] recalled due to [[hepatitis A]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/hepatitis-strawberries-california-fda/#:~:text=Packages%20of%20FreshKampo%20and%20HEB,California%2C%20federal%20food%20regulators%20said. | title=Strawberries likely caused hepatitis a outbreak, FDA says | website=[[CBS News]] | date=8 June 2022 }}</ref><ref>[https://www.washingtonpost.com/nation/2022/05/30/hepatitis-a-strawberries-outbreak-fda/ Hepatitis a strawberries outbreak: FDA] ''The Washington Post'' (subscription required)</ref>

* USA: June: [[Costco]] recalled 400,000 solar powered umbrellas after the lithium-ion batteries would overheat and ignite.
* USA: August: the Huffy Corporation issued a recall for thousands of its ''[[Blue's Clues & You!]]'' ride-on toys after multiple children were injured while using the toy. All of the units affected by the recall were sold at Walmart stores nationwide.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.wagmtv.com/2022/08/27/recall-issued-blues-clues-riding-toy-after-children-suffer-facial-injuries/|title=Recall issued for 'Blue's Clues' riding toy after children suffer facial injuries|date=August 27, 2022|access-date=April 1, 2023|website=WAGM TV|language=en}}</ref>

* USA: February 1: Conagra Brands issued a major recall of nearly 2.6 million pounds of canned meat and poultry due to a packaging defect that may cause the food to get contaminated.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/conagra-brands-recalls-nearly-2-6-million-pounds-of-canned-meat-and-poultry/|title=Conagra Brands recalls nearly 2.6 million pounds of canned meat and poultry|date=February 1, 2023|access-date=April 1, 2023|website=CBS News|language=en}}</ref>
* USA: February 9: Colgate-Palmolive issued a recall of nearly 5 million bottles of Fabuloso multi-purpose cleaner due to a risk of bacterial growth.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cnn.com/2023/02/09/business/fabuloso-cleaner-recall/index.html|title=About 5 million bottles of Fabuloso recalled because of bacterial contamination|date=February 9, 2023|access-date=April 1, 2023|website=CNN|language=en}}</ref>
* USA: February 20: 300,000 bottles of Starbucks bottled Frappuccinos were recalled due to possibly containing pieces of glass in them.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.npr.org/starbucks-frappuccino-recall-fda|title=Bottled of Starbucks Frappuccinos may contain glass and have been recalled|date=February 20, 2023|access-date=April 1, 2023|website=NPR|language=en}}</ref>
* USA: March 10: More than 3.2 million units of Calico Critters toys were recalled after two children died from choking on the baby bottle and pacifier accessories, posing a serious choking hazard for other small children that may choke and die from the product.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cnn.com/2023/03/09/business/3-2-million-calico-critters-toys-recall/index.html|title=More than 3.2 million Calico Critters toys recalled after deaths of two children|date=March 10, 2023|access-date=April 1, 2023|website=CNN|language=en}}</ref>
* USA: March 18: Strawberry products that were sold at Costco, ALDI, Trader Joe's, KeHE, Vital Choice Seafood, and PCC Community Markets stores were recalled due to hepatitis A.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.npr.org/2023/03/18/1164557863/strawberry-recall-fda-costco-trader-joes-aldi|title=Strawberry products sold at Costco, Trader Joe's, recalled after hepatitis A outbreak|date=March 18, 2023|access-date=April 1, 2023|website=NPR|language=en}}</ref>
* USA: March 24: More than 3,000 pounds of boneless beef chuck products that were distributed to several states were recalled due to possible contamination of E. coli.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.foxbusiness.com/lifestyle/meat-recalled-possible-e-coli-contamination|title=Over 3K pounds of meat recalled over possible E. coli contamination|date=March 24, 2023|access-date=April 1, 2023|website=Fox Business|language=en}}</ref>
* USA: March 28: Honda issued a major recall of more than 330,000 vehicles due to a mirror issue with the cars, with the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration stating that the vehicles did not comply with rear visibility requirements.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nbcnews.com/business/autos/honda-recalls-330000-vehicles-mirror-issue-could-lead-to-crash-rcna77002|title=Honda recalls more than 330,000 vehicles due to mirror issue|date=March 28, 2023|access-date=April 1, 2023|website=NBC News|language=en}}</ref>
* USA: March 30: [[Jeep]] recalled over 57,000 of its Jeep Wranglers over an unnecessary part that could cause a fuel leak and a fire to the product.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/money/cars/2023/03/30/jeep-wrangler-recall-fuel-leak/11572072002/|title=57,000 Jeep Wranglers recalled over 'unnecessary' part that could cause fuel leak, fire|date=March 30, 2023|access-date=April 2, 2023|website=USA Today|language=en}}</ref>
* USA: March 30: [[Carhartt]] recalled more than 32,000 pairs of its pants because they posed a trip hazard to the person who would wear the pants. The units were sold at [[Dick's Sporting Goods]] stores nationwide and online from July 2022 through November 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://fox59.com/news/mens-carhartt-pants-recalled-over-trip-hazard/|title=Men's Carhartt pants recalled over trip hazard|date=March 30, 2023|access-date=April 2, 2023|website=Fox 59|language=en}}</ref>
* USA: March 31: [[Tesla, Inc.|Tesla]] issued a major recall of its electric Semi trucks because the parking brake may not engage when applied by the driver, which may cause car accidents.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cnn.com/2023/03/31/business/tesla-semi-recall/index.html|title=The Tesla Semi is getting recalled for faulty parking brakes|date=March 31, 2023|access-date=April 1, 2023|website=CNN|language=en}}</ref>
* USA: March 31: [[Unilever]] issued a recall for over 800,000 units of Laundress fabric conditioner over a carcinogen hazard.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.foxbusiness.com/lifestyle/laundress-recalls-fabric-conditioner-chemical-hazard|title=The Laundress recalls fabric conditioner over carcinogen hazard|date=March 31, 2023|access-date=April 1, 2023|website=Fox Business|language=en}}</ref>

* USA: August 6: [[Frito-Lay]] recalls 7,000 Doritos bags over soy, wheat allergen problems.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/brucelee/2023/08/06/fda-frito-lay-recalls-2-sizes-of-doritos-nacho-cheese-flavored-tortilla-chips/|title=FDA: Frito-Lay Recalls 2 Sizes Of Doritos Nacho Cheese Flavored Tortilla Chips|date=August 6, 2023|access-date=August 6, 2023|website=Forbes|language=en}}</ref>
